# Forbidden-operation noninvocation 5.0.0

This certification admits `proof.operation.forbidden-noninvocation@5.0.0`.

The guarantee concerns the declared proof model: one exact subject MUST_NOT call
any member of one complete, nonempty forbidden-operation population while the
declared context applies. A call to even one member contradicts that prohibition.
The verification reads the exact subject, context, population and every member;
its positive-calls falsifier retains those same bindings. This does not forbid
every dependency or consumption relationship.

Certification executes synthetic model controls, not arbitrary target code. It
does not establish actual execution or mutation outcomes, truthful grounding,
unmodeled dynamic/reflection/environment calls, undeclared operations, calls
outside the context, or production call-graph discovery.

The full census binds current authored profile weakenings and substantive rejection
cases. The prohibition modality has no independent valid broadening under the
current positive-falsifier policy; certification mechanically checks that closed
domain. Permission in place of prohibition, optional verification, and retired
recommendations remain explicit rejection controls. The optional-verification
witness retains an independent mandatory verification of narrower observation
coverage so native graph validity does not substitute for this proof’s exact
mandatory observation requirement. Controls include three unrelated domains, permitted calls, first and last
single-member forbidden calls, whole-population calls, subject/context isolation,
complete population bindings, and mismatched or retired broad-use declarations.
